artifacts.summary: All five plan phases implemented and verified: shared validate_shake_result()/run_and_validate_shake() helper, --list guard-hoist fix, --self-test subcommand with four fixtures, reconciled header, and full-gate live verification.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed scripts/check-shake-residue.sh --list's false-clean defect by consolidating both fatal shake-result conditions into a shared validate_shake_result()/run_and_validate_shake() helper (mirroring check-axiom-census.sh), rewiring all three usage modes onto it, adding a --self-test subcommand with four fixtures (including the literal reproduced stale-target regression), and reconciling the EXIT-CODE CONTRACT header.

memory_candidates.content: For bash ratchet/gate scripts that wrap an external tool with a 0/1/2-style exit-code contract across multiple usage modes (--list/--update/bare), consolidate the fatal-condition checks into one shared validator function composed with the impure tool-invocation function, rather than duplicating the guard per mode. check-axiom-census.sh's run_and_validate_census() is the in-tree template; check-shake-residue.sh's --list guard-hoist defect was caused by exactly this kind of duplication drifting out of sync. Keep the pure validation logic (reads globals, returns 0/2, never calls exit) as a function separate from the impure runner, so a --self-test-style fixture can call the validator directly without invoking the real external tool.

For a bash self-test subcommand that injects captured fixture output in place of a real external-tool call, add an env-var short-circuit at the top of the impure runner function (e.g. SHAKE_SELF_TEST_FIXTURE) that populates the same output globals a real run would, and use a SECOND env var to redirect any ratchet/baseline file the script would write (e.g. SHAKE_SELF_TEST_BASELINE) so subprocess end-to-end assertions can never clobber the real baseline. Assert the real baseline is byte-identical before/after the self-test as a hard requirement, not a nicety. When asserting 'zero bytes of stdout' from a subprocess, capture to a real file and use wc -c -- command substitution silently strips trailing newlines and will hide a stray blank-line regression.
